findings.title: Feed and remote content is stored as unsanitized HTML and rendered as-is
findings.description: `TopicEmbed.import` creates posts with `cook_method: raw_html` (topic_embed.rb:22). `Post#cook` then returns `raw` unchanged (app/models/post.rb:133), so neither the markdown pipeline nor a sanitizer runs. The feed path does no sanitization of its own: `PollFeed#poll_feed` runs `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` (app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:35), which turns escaped feed text such as `<script>` into live markup. The `import_remote` path does pass through ruby-readability with a tag and attribute allowlist (topic_embed.rb:48-50), but the feed path does not. The stored HTML is output unescaped in two places: the normal topic view (`app/assets/javascripts/discourse/templates/post.js.handlebars:70`, `{{{cooked}}}`) and the embed page (`app/views/embed/best.html.erb:19`, `raw post.cooked`). Anyone who reads the topic, or loads the embed page, runs the script on the forum origin. The feed content is third-party, so a feed author or a compromised feed can supply the payload. There is a second injection point. `topic_embed.rb:13` interpolates `url` into `#{url}` without escaping. The URL only has to match `^https?://` (poll_feed.rb:33, topic_embed.rb:11), so a `'` in it can break out of the attribute. Anonymous callers can reach this too. `EmbedController#best` enqueues a fetch of whatever `embed_url` the caller supplies (embed_controller.rb:15), and the host check compares only the hostname (topic_retriever.rb:14-19). If the embeddable site returns 200 for the crafted path, the value is written into the footer. Whether the attribute break becomes executable depends on how Nokogiri re-serializes it in `absolutize_urls` (topic_embed.rb:56-75). I did not run that. No spec covers sanitization. `spec/models/topic_embed_spec.rb` asserts the raw passthrough (`post.cooked.should == post.raw`).

findings.title: embed.js and embed.css are not precompiled, so they will 404 in production
findings.description: `app/assets/javascripts/embed.js` and `app/assets/stylesheets/embed.css.scss` are not in `config.assets.precompile`. The additions are images (config/application.rb:57-59), a fixed list (line 61), `defer/*`, and `locales/*`. Production sets `config.assets.compile = false` and `digest = true` (config/environments/production.rb:23,26), so Sprockets will not compile `/assets/embed.js` on request. The host page's `<script src=".../assets/embed.js">` will 404. The layout's `stylesheet_link_tag 'embed'` (app/views/layouts/embed.html.erb:4) will point at a missing asset, leaving the embed page unstyled. Tests run with `compile = true` (config/environments/test.rb:40), so the suite will not catch this.

findings.title: Anonymous embed requests can trigger unbounded feed and page fetches
findings.description: For every unauthenticated request whose embed URL has no topic, `EmbedController#best` enqueues `retrieve_topic` (embed_controller.rb:15). The request has no rate limit. The 60-second throttle is keyed on the full, unnormalized URL (topic_retriever.rb:26), so `?x=1`, `?x=2`, and so on each get a fresh key. Each job that gets through runs `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` synchronously when feed polling is enabled (topic_retriever.rb:40-42). That downloads the whole feed and imports every item. It then fetches the page (line 45). The throttle also uses `setnx` followed by a separate `expire` (lines 27-28). A crash between the two leaves a key with no TTL, which blocks that URL permanently. Use an atomic set-with-TTL, and throttle feed polling separately from per-URL retrieval.

findings.title: PollFeed aborts on the first failing item, and the success check does not verify persistence
findings.description: `poll_feed` has no per-item rescue (poll_feed.rb:31-37), so one exception ends the run. `PostCreator#create` returns `@post` even when the transaction was rolled back (lib/post_creator.rb:222-236, return at line 86). An unsaved post is still `present?`, so `TopicEmbed.create!` runs with `post_id: nil` and violates the `null: false` constraint (db/migrate/20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb:3-6). Other failures also raise. `embed_url` is a `varchar(255)` (migration line 6), so a long feed link fails the insert. `i.content` is nil for an item with no description (poll_feed.rb:35), assuming SimpleRSS returns nil for missing elements; I did not confirm that against the gem. The `PostRevisor` nil case (below) also raises. Check `post.persisted?`, rescue and log per item, and continue.

findings.title: The import transaction defeats PostCreator's enqueue-after-commit ordering
findings.description: `TopicEmbed.import` wraps `PostCreator.create` in `Topic.transaction` (topic_embed.rb:21). `PostCreator#create` calls `enqueue_jobs` (post_creator.rb:85), which triggers `process_post`, before the outer transaction commits. The comment at post_creator.rb:290-291 says jobs must be enqueued after commit for this reason. In production, `Jobs.enqueue` pushes to Sidekiq immediately (app/jobs/base.rb:162-167), so the job can run before the post is visible. If `TopicEmbed.create!` then fails, the job refers to a post that was rolled back.

findings.title: A trashed embedded post makes re-import crash and blocks later feed items
findings.description: `TopicEmbed` has `belongs_to :post`, and `Post` has a default scope from `Trashable` (lib/trashable.rb:5). Once the post is trashed, `embed.post` returns nil. If the feed content has changed, `PostRevisor.new(nil).revise!` raises NoMethodError (topic_embed.rb:34-36). Combined with the missing per-item rescue, one trashed post blocks every feed item after it on every hourly run. Handle the nil case by skipping or recreating the post, and log it.

findings.title: absolutize_urls rewrites protocol-relative URLs into broken paths
findings.description: `href.start_with?('/')` also matches `//cdn.example.com/a.png`. The code then builds `"#{prefix}/#{href.sub(/^\/+/, '')}"`, which strips all leading slashes. The link becomes `http://blog.example.com/cdn.example.com/a.png`. Protocol-relative URLs should keep their host and get only the scheme (`"#{uri.scheme}:#{href}"`). The same bug is at line 71 for `img src`.

findings.title: Editing an imported post keeps unsanitized HTML cooking
findings.description: `cook_method` is never reset. `before_save` calls `cook(raw)` on every update (post.rb:319-321), so once a post is `raw_html`, any later edit keeps it. Markdown the editor sends, such as `**bold**`, is stored and rendered as raw HTML. `Plugin::Filter.apply(:after_post_cook, ...)` is skipped too. Raw-HTML status is therefore sticky per post, and no code path clears it. Reset it on user-initiated revisions, or keep raw-HTML posts out of the editable path.

findings.title: The Disqus import drops `--category`, aborts on one bad link, and duplicates comments on re-run
findings.description:
Three behavior changes are not mentioned in the change:
- The `--category` option is removed, so `-c` now fails with a Thor unknown-option error. The category logic is gone with no replacement.
- `TopicEmbed.import_remote` is called once per thread, with a blocking HTTP fetch and no rescue. One 404 or network error aborts the whole import. The `ensure` only restores settings.
- `TopicEmbed.import` returns the existing `embed.post` when the topic already exists (topic_embed.rb:32). `if post.present?` is then true on a re-run, so every Disqus comment is created again on the existing topic. Before this change, a re-run created a new topic.

The topic's `created_at` is no longer set either.

findings.title: Migration drops tables with force: true, and an already-applied migration was edited
findings.description: `create_table :topic_embeds, force: true` drops an existing `topic_embeds` table before creating it, so running this against a database that already has the table destroys its rows. Nothing needs `force`. The same change adds `force: true` to the existing migration `db/migrate/20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb:3`. Environments that already ran it will not re-run it, so the edit has no effect there. Remove both, and use a new migration for any schema change.

findings.title: Gemfile adds two gems that the default lockfile does not contain
findings.description: `ruby-readability` and `simple-rss` appear in `Gemfile_rails4.lock` (lines 313 and 344) but not in `Gemfile.lock` or `Gemfile_rails_master.lock`. `bundle install --deployment` or `--frozen` against the default lockfile will fail. The lazy `require 'simple-rss'` and `require 'ruby-readability'` calls (poll_feed.rb:28, topic_embed.rb:45) will not load there. `*.lock` was excluded from the diff range, so I could not see whether this commit touched the lockfiles. This describes HEAD. Confirm which lockfile the deploy uses.

findings.title: The embed.js origin check is a substring test
findings.description: `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1` accepts any origin that is a substring of `discourseUrl`. If the forum is `https://forum.example.com/`, a sender at `https://forum.example.co` passes. That sender can then set the iframe height (lines 17-21). Compare `e.origin` for equality with the parsed origin of `discourseUrl`, and check `e.source === iframe.contentWindow`. The impact is limited to height changes, not script injection.

findings.title: The embed view's `end if` closer is unusual, and no spec renders the view
findings.description: `<%- end if %>` closes the `if` with a dangling modifier. No other file in `app/views` uses this form. Whether ERB's trim handling makes it parse depends on the trailing newline, and I could not render the template in this session. `embed_controller_spec.rb` does not use `render_views`, so nothing in the suite renders this view. Replace it with `<%- end %>`, and add a request or view spec that renders both branches.

findings.title: The specs miss the core behavior, and some mock what they test
findings.description:
- `poll_feed_spec.rb` checks only the guard conditions, and it mocks `poll_feed` (line 35). Item parsing, the `i.id` fallback, and the import loop have no coverage.
- Nothing covers the Redis throttle (`retrieved_recently?`), `fetch_http`, `import_remote`, protocol-relative URLs, or the footer escaping.
- `spec/components/topic_retriever_spec.rb` stubs private methods (`retrieved_recently?`, `perform_retrieve`) with mocha, so it tests call structure rather than behavior.
- `spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb:35-38` puts assertions in an `after` hook, so they run after every example, including failing ones.
- The example at `embed_controller_spec.rb:8` is named "is 404" but asserts only `should_not be_success`. The catch-all `rescue_from Exception` (application_controller.rb:39) decides the actual response.

findings.title: Dead code and a duplicated lookup
findings.description:
- `PollFeed#feed_key` (lines 20-22) has no callers in the repo. A grep finds only its definition.
- `app/jobs/regular/retrieve_topic.rb:1` requires `email/sender`, which the file never uses.
- The `embed_by_username` user lookup is duplicated at poll_feed.rb:25 and topic_retriever.rb:49.

findings.title: X-Frame-Options "ALLOWALL" is not a valid value
findings.description: Browsers recognize DENY, SAMEORIGIN, and ALLOW-FROM. An unrecognized value is ignored, so this only works by omission. Nothing else in `app/` sets X-Frame-Options, so the line changes nothing else. Remove it and document that framing is intentional, or use a CSP `frame-ancestors` directive. The spec at embed_controller_spec.rb:37 locks in the invalid value.

findings.title: The layout puts request.referer into a JavaScript string with HTML escaping
findings.description: `'<%= request.referer %>'` is HTML-escaped, which is not a JavaScript-safe encoding. I did not find a practical break-out, but the safety depends on escaping details. Use `<%= j request.referer %>`, or compute the origin on the server from the verified host.

findings.title: PostCreator reads cook_method outside its explicit option list
findings.description: Other pass-through options go through the list at line 212, but `cook_method` is read directly from `@opts`. It is not reachable over HTTP today. `PostsController#create` passes only what `create_params` permits (posts_controller.rb:226-254). Any future caller that forwards unfiltered options could choose the cooking pipeline. Consider a dedicated internal path for importers so that the choice does not live in the general options hash.

findings.title: Kernel#open is used with URLs that come from user-supplied input
findings.description: `open(url)` resolves to `Kernel#open` for strings that do not start with a URI scheme. On Ruby before 3.0, a string starting with `|` runs as a shell command. `import_remote` receives a link taken from the Disqus XML (lib/tasks/disqus.thor:148), and poll_feed.rb:29 opens the configured feed URL. Use `URI.parse(url).open`, which only opens URIs.

findings.title: Import mutates its contents argument
findings.description: `contents << "..."` appends the footer to the caller's string, so a caller that reuses the string sees the footer. Build a new string instead.

findings.title: Whitespace-only changes are mixed into the feature
findings.description: This migration has trailing whitespace removed and a newline added at EOF. `lib/post_revisor.rb:13` loses a blank line, and disqus.thor has a stray blank line at 147. Split these out of the feature change so the review and blame history stay focused.

findings.title: The embed endpoint enforces topic visibility
findings.description: `TopicView` calls `guardian.ensure_can_see!(@topic)` (lib/topic_view.rb:306), and `EmbedController#best` builds the view with the caller's `current_user`. A caller who supplies an `embed_url` for a restricted or private topic does not get its posts. The `Post` default scope and the guardian check together keep the endpoint within the same read rules as the topic page.
